title: The Trail of Toasted Oat
story: The game of fetch transitioned seamlessly into a game of follow-the-leader. Pippin did not run far; he only ran far enough to ensure James's small hands were empty of the pinecone. A short trot, a sharp bark, and a look back. A short trot, a sharp bark, and a look back. James, adjusting the leather strap of his canister, understood the silent invitation. He followed the toasted-oat colored dog down the damp stone steps of the Terrace Gardens, leaving the wild ferns behind. Down the moss-covered steps they went, where the mist still hung low in the branches. Down the narrow cobblestone alleyways they went, where the smell of woodsmoke and freshly baked tortillas began to drift from cozy kitchens. Down the path of a bright blue stucco wall they went, where rain-streaked window panes reflected the soft morning sky. Pippin moved with absolute certainty, his tail a steady, joyful metronome guiding James deeper into a quiet residential neighborhood of Oakhaven. Pippin finally stopped in front of a modest wooden gate, scratching at the base until it creaked open to reveal a small, flower-filled courtyard. In the center of the courtyard sat a young girl named Sofia, who was busy rinsing clay pots of geraniums. When she saw Pippin, her face lit up. When she saw James perched on the low wall beside her dog, her eyes widened in quiet wonder. She did not shout or run; instead, she reached into her pocket and held out a small, dried slice of sweet potato. James looked at the girl, then at Pippin, who had happily curled up at her feet. He touched the brass magnifying lens hanging from his neck, feeling the familiar warmth of his accumulated treasures. He took a cautious step onto the courtyard flagstones, his small fingers reaching out to accept the offering as the morning sun warmed his back.
